questions.q: What obstacle do Msimangu and Kumalo meet at the bus rank for Alexandra?
choices: The buses are cancelled by a strike of drivers
A boycott of the buses — people refuse to ride until the fare is brought back to fourpence
questions.explain: A man persuades them not to ride: 'If you use this bus you are weakening the cause of the black people.'

questions.q: Who is the man organising the boycott at the bus rank?
choices: Dubula — 'the famous Dubula', said to have 'the heart'
questions.explain: They say Tomlinson has the brains and John the voice, but Dubula has the heart; he has given up his own work to picket the buses.

questions.q: How far is it to walk to Alexandra?
questions.explain: People of all ages, some sick or crippled, are walking it daily — starting at four in the morning.

questions.q: How do Msimangu and Kumalo actually get most of the way to Alexandra?
choices: They take the bus after all
A white man stops his car and gives them a lift, then drives back to Johannesburg
The police give them a lift
questions.explain: Many white people are stopping to carry the walking people, especially the old and the crippled.

questions.q: Why did white residents get up a petition to do away with Alexandra altogether?
choices: Because of crime — an old white woman died of shock after a bag-snatch, and a white woman was killed resisting robbers
Because the land was needed for mining
questions.explain: Their white friends fought the petition, arguing the good of Alexandra — owning a house, a place of one's own — outweighed the bad.

questions.q: At 79 Twenty-Third Avenue, what does Mrs Mkize first tell them?
choices: That Absalom and another Kumalo (John's son) left about a year ago, talking of many places
That she has never heard of Absalom
questions.explain: There is 'fear in her eyes'; Msimangu sends Kumalo on ahead and returns alone.

questions.q: What does Msimangu get Mrs Mkize to admit, after swearing to her on the Bible?
choices: That the two young men brought stolen goods to the house at night — clothes, watches, money — and left when 'near to being discovered'
That Absalom has already been hanged
questions.explain: She never saw blood on them, 'umfundisi' — 'only a little, but something.'

questions.q: Whom does Mrs Mkize name as a friend of the young men who might know where they went?
questions.explain: 'They were friendly with the taxi-driver Hlabeni. Near the bus rank he lives.'

questions.q: Where does Hlabeni say Absalom has gone?
choices: To Orlando, to live among the squatters in Shanty Town
questions.explain: He suggests asking the Municipality people who work among the squatters and know them all.

questions.q: What exchange on the road, involving a white man carrying black passengers, leaves Msimangu saying 'That is what beats me'?
choices: A traffic officer says he is carrying passengers on a bus route, and the white man answers, 'Then take me to court'
The white man refuses to stop
The passengers refuse to get in
questions.explain: Msimangu hits himself across the chest, repeating 'Take me to court' — astonished by such open defiance in a white man on the black people's behalf.
